concept_summary: Arista EOS uses Cisco IOS-like CLI syntax by design for easy migration but runs on Linux underneath. Initial setup includes hostname, management interface, user accounts, and ZTP (Zero Touch Provisioning) configuration. EOS emphasizes automation with extensive API support including eAPI REST interface. Configuration changes take effect immediately.
cli_mode_context: Enter configuration mode with 'configure' or 'config terminal'. Use IOS-style commands. Access underlying Linux with 'bash' command for advanced troubleshooting.
example_commands:
configure
hostname DC1-Leaf-01
ip domain-name example.com
interface Management1
 ip address 192.0.2.10/24
 no shutdown
username admin privilege 15 role network-admin secret Str0ngP@ss
banner motd
Arista DC1-Leaf-01 - Authorized Access Only
EOF
management api http-commands
 protocol https
 no shutdown
end
write memory

key_parameters.description: Creates user with full admin privileges
Saves running config to startup config

concept_summary: EOS interfaces follow Cisco naming conventions (Ethernet, Port-Channel, Vlan, Loopback) with configuration syntax nearly identical to IOS. Interfaces support routed (no switchport) or switched modes. Configuration includes speed, duplex, descriptions, and L2/L3 parameters. EOS excels at high-density 100G/400G interfaces with advanced buffering and telemetry.
cli_mode_context: Configure interfaces with 'interface <type><number>' in config mode. Use 'no switchport' for Layer 3 mode. Multiple interface ranges supported.
example_commands:
configure
interface Ethernet1
 description Spine-Uplink
 no switchport
 ip address 192.0.2.1/30
 mtu 9214
 no shutdown
interface Ethernet2
 description Server-Port
 switchport mode access
 switchport access vlan 100
 spanning-tree portfast
 no shutdown
interface Vlan100
 description SVI-for-Servers
 ip address 198.51.100.1/24
 ip virtual-router address 198.51.100.254
interface Loopback0
 ip address 192.0.2.100/32
end

key_parameters.description: Converts port to Layer 3 routed mode
Assigns IPv4 address with CIDR notation

concept_summary: EOS VLANs use standard 802.1Q with IOS-like configuration. VLAN database supports 4094 VLANs. Trunk and access ports follow IOS conventions. SVI (VLAN interfaces) provide inter-VLAN routing. EOS adds virtual-router MAC for consistent gateway across MLAG pairs. Rapid-PVST+ or MST provide loop prevention.
cli_mode_context: Create VLANs with 'vlan <id>' in config mode. Configure trunk/access on interfaces. Create SVIs with 'interface Vlan<id>'.
example_commands:
configure
vlan 10
 name Engineering
vlan 20
 name Sales  
vlan 100
 name Servers
interface Ethernet10
 description Access-Port-Engineering
 switchport mode access
 switchport access vlan 10
 spanning-tree portfast
interface Ethernet48
 description Trunk-to-Distribution
 switchport mode trunk
 switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,20,100
 switchport trunk native vlan 999
interface Vlan10
 ip address 192.0.2.1/24
interface Vlan20
 ip address 198.51.100.1/24
spanning-tree mode rapid-pvst
end

concept_summary: EOS static routes use IOS syntax with destination, mask, next-hop or interface, and administrative distance. IPv4 and IPv6 static routes supported. VRF-aware routing enables multi-tenancy. Track objects provide conditional routing based on reachability. Static routes integrate with BFD for fast failure detection.
cli_mode_context: Configure static routes with 'ip route' in config mode. Specify destination, mask, next-hop/interface, and optional distance.
example_commands:
configure
ip route 0.0.0.0/0 192.0.2.1
ip route 198.51.100.0/24 Ethernet1
ip route 203.0.113.0/24 192.0.2.5 10
ip route 203.0.113.128/25 Null0
ipv6 route ::/0 2001:DB8::1
ip route vrf CUSTOMER-A 10.0.0.0/8 198.51.100.1
end

concept_summary: EOS OSPF implements OSPFv2 and OSPFv3 with area hierarchy and IOS-like syntax. Configuration includes process ID, router ID, network statements, and area parameters. EOS adds BFD integration for sub-second failover. Supports authentication, graceful restart, and ECMP. Multi-instance OSPF per VRF.
cli_mode_context: Enable OSPF with 'router ospf <process-id>' in config mode. Use 'network' statements or interface-level configuration.
example_commands:
configure
router ospf 1
 router-id 192.0.2.1
 network 192.0.2.0/24 area 0.0.0.0
 network 198.51.100.0/24 area 0.0.0.10
 passive-interface default
 no passive-interface Ethernet1
 max-lsas 12000
 distance ospf external 110
interface Ethernet1
 ip ospf network point-to-point
 ip ospf cost 100
 ip ospf area 0.0.0.0
 ip ospf bfd
end

concept_summary: EOS BGP supports IBGP, EBGP, and advanced features like route reflection, confederation, and add-path. Configuration uses IOS syntax with neighbor statements and address families. EOS excels at large-scale BGP with EVPN for data center fabrics. Supports diverse AFIs including IPv4, IPv6, EVPN, and VPNv4. BGP unnumbered simplifies configuration using IPv6 link-local addressing.
cli_mode_context: Configure BGP with 'router bgp <as-number>' in config mode. Define neighbors and activate address families.
example_commands:
configure
router bgp 65001
 router-id 192.0.2.1
 neighbor 198.51.100.1 remote-as 65002
 neighbor 198.51.100.1 description EBGP-ISP
 neighbor 192.0.2.254 remote-as 65001
 neighbor 192.0.2.254 update-source Loopback0
 neighbor 192.0.2.254 next-hop-self
 network 192.0.2.0/24
 address-family ipv4
  neighbor 198.51.100.1 activate
  neighbor 192.0.2.254 activate
 address-family evpn
  neighbor 192.0.2.254 activate
  neighbor 192.0.2.254 send-community extended
end

concept_summary: EOS does not support EIGRP as it is Cisco proprietary. IS-IS support is available for service provider deployments with Level-1/Level-2 hierarchy. RIP exists for legacy compatibility. Modern EOS deployments favor OSPF and BGP especially for EVPN-VXLAN data center fabrics.
cli_mode_context: Configure IS-IS with 'router isis' if needed. Most modern deployments use BGP for underlay/overlay.
example_commands:
configure
router isis CORE
 net 49.0001.0192.0000.2001.00
 is-type level-2
 address-family ipv4 unicast
interface Ethernet1
 isis enable CORE
 isis network point-to-point
end
reason: EIGRP not supported (Cisco proprietary). IS-IS available but uncommon in EOS deployments focused on data center BGP/EVPN. RIP exists but legacy only.

concept_summary: EOS supports VRRP for first-hop redundancy with virtual IP addressing. MLAG (Multi-Chassis Link Aggregation) provides more comprehensive HA by allowing active-active forwarding across switch pairs. Virtual ARP enables anycast gateway for VXLAN environments. VRRP configuration follows standard RFC with priorities and preemption.
cli_mode_context: Configure VRRP under interface with 'vrrp <group>' commands. MLAG configured separately under 'mlag configuration'.
example_commands:
configure
interface Vlan10
 ip address 192.0.2.2/24
 vrrp 1 priority 110
 vrrp 1 ip 192.0.2.1
 vrrp 1 preempt delay minimum 60
interface Vlan20
 ip address 198.51.100.2/24
 ip virtual-router address 198.51.100.1
mlag configuration
 domain-id MLAG-PAIR
 local-interface Vlan4094
 peer-address 10.255.255.2
 peer-link Port-Channel1
end

concept_summary: EOS ACLs use IOS syntax with standard and extended lists for traffic filtering. ACLs match on Layer 3/4 headers with permit/deny actions. IPv4 and IPv6 ACLs supported. Control-plane ACL protects management plane. EOS adds object-groups and time-based ACLs. Applied to interfaces, line VTY, or control-plane.
cli_mode_context: Create ACLs with 'ip access-list' in config mode. Apply to interfaces with 'ip access-group'. Use sequence numbers for ordering.
example_commands:
configure
ip access-list standard MGMT-ACCESS
 10 permit 192.0.2.0/24
 20 deny any log
ip access-list extended BLOCK-TELNET
 10 deny tcp any any eq telnet log
 20 permit ip any any
interface Ethernet10
 ip access-group BLOCK-TELNET in
line vty 0 4
 access-class MGMT-ACCESS in
ipv6 access-list IPV6-FILTER
 10 deny ipv6 any any fragments
 20 permit ipv6 2001:DB8::/32 any
 30 deny ipv6 any any log
end

concept_summary: EOS NAT supports source NAT, destination NAT, and static NAT for address translation. Configuration includes NAT pools, inside/outside interfaces, and translation rules. PAT provides port translation for address conservation. NAT integrates with VRF for multi-tenancy. Dynamic NAT with overload most common for Internet access.
cli_mode_context: Configure NAT with 'ip nat' commands. Define inside/outside interfaces and translation rules.
example_commands:
configure
ip nat pool PUBLIC-POOL 198.51.100.10 198.51.100.20 prefix-length 28
ip access-list standard NAT-INTERNAL
 permit 192.0.2.0/24
ip nat inside source list NAT-INTERNAL pool PUBLIC-POOL overload
ip nat inside source static 192.0.2.10 198.51.100.50
interface Vlan10
 ip nat inside
interface Ethernet1
 ip nat outside
end

concept_summary: EOS supports IPsec VPN for site-to-site connectivity with IKEv1/IKEv2. Configuration includes crypto maps, IKE policies, transform sets, and access lists defining interesting traffic. Both tunnel and transport modes supported. Integration with dynamic routing over VPN. CloudVision provides centralized VPN management.
cli_mode_context: Configure IPsec with 'crypto' commands similar to IOS. Define IKE policy, transform set, crypto map, and apply to interface.
example_commands:
configure
crypto isakmp policy 10
 encryption aes 256
 hash sha256
 authentication pre-share
 group 14
crypto isakmp key MyPreSharedKey address 203.0.113.1
crypto ipsec transform-set STRONG esp-aes 256 esp-sha256-hmac
ip access-list extended VPN-TRAFFIC
 permit ip 192.0.2.0/24 198.51.100.0/24
crypto map SITE-TO-SITE 10 ipsec-isakmp
 set peer 203.0.113.1
 set transform-set STRONG
 match address VPN-TRAFFIC
interface Ethernet1
 crypto map SITE-TO-SITE
end

concept_summary: EOS QoS uses modular framework with class-maps, policy-maps, and service-policies. Hardware-based QoS leverages merchant silicon capabilities. Configuration includes classification, marking, policing, shaping, and queueing. DSCP-based and CoS-based QoS supported. EOS provides granular queue control with weighted round-robin and strict priority.
cli_mode_context: Define class-maps for classification, policy-maps for actions, apply with service-policy to interfaces.
example_commands:
configure
class-map match-any VOICE
 match ip dscp ef
class-map match-any CRITICAL
 match ip dscp af31
policy-map QOS-OUT
 class VOICE
  priority level 1
  police rate 2 mbps
 class CRITICAL
  bandwidth percent 40
 class class-default
  bandwidth percent 20
interface Ethernet1
 service-policy output QOS-OUT
qos cos 5
end

concept_summary: EOS supports local and remote AAA using TACACS+ or RADIUS with fallback to local accounts. Role-based access control provides command authorization. Integration with LDAP for user authentication. API authentication supports token-based access. Accounting logs user actions to remote servers. Multi-factor authentication available.
cli_mode_context: Configure AAA with 'aaa' commands. Define TACACS+/RADIUS servers and method lists.
example_commands:
configure
tacacs-server host 192.0.2.50 key TacacsSecret123
tacacs-server host 192.0.2.51 key TacacsSecret123
aaa authentication login default group tacacs+ local
aaa authorization exec default group tacacs+ local
aaa authorization commands all default group tacacs+ local
aaa accounting commands all default start-stop group tacacs+
aaa accounting exec default start-stop group tacacs+
end

key_parameters.description: Try TACACS+ then fall back to local

concept_summary: EOS supports SNMP v1, v2c, and v3 for monitoring with MIB support and trap generation. Logging to console, buffer, and remote syslog servers with severity filtering. Streaming telemetry with gNMI and OpenConfig for real-time monitoring. CloudVision provides centralized monitoring and analytics. EOS agent extensions enable custom monitoring.
cli_mode_context: Configure SNMP with 'snmp-server' commands and logging with 'logging' commands.
example_commands:
configure
snmp-server community PublicRO ro
snmp-server community PrivateRW rw
snmp-server location DataCenter-01
snmp-server contact netops@example.com
snmp-server host 192.0.2.100 version 2c PublicRO
snmp-server enable traps
logging console warnings
logging buffered 100000 informational
logging host 192.0.2.200
logging source-interface Loopback0
logging facility local7
service timestamps log datetime localtime
end

key_parameters.description: Enables buffer with size and level

concept_summary: EOS excels at VXLAN-EVPN for data center fabrics with BGP EVPN control plane. VXLAN provides Layer 2 overlay over Layer 3 underlay using UDP encapsulation. EVPN distributes MAC/IP information via BGP. Configuration includes VXLAN interface (Vxlan1), VNI mappings, and BGP EVPN address family. Anycast gateway provides distributed first-hop redundancy. Multi-tenancy through VRF-aware VXLAN.
cli_mode_context: Configure VXLAN under 'interface Vxlan1'. Map VLANs to VNIs. Enable EVPN in BGP. Configure anycast gateway.
example_commands:
configure
interface Vxlan1
 vxlan source-interface Loopback0
 vxlan udp-port 4789
 vxlan vlan 100 vni 10100
 vxlan vlan 200 vni 10200
 vxlan vrf TENANT-A vni 50001
interface Loopback0
 ip address 192.0.2.1/32
vlan 100
 name Web-Tier
vlan 200
 name App-Tier
interface Vlan100
 ip address virtual 198.51.100.1/24
interface Vlan200
 ip address virtual 203.0.113.1/24
ip virtual-router mac-address 00:1c:73:00:00:01
router bgp 65001
 neighbor 192.0.2.254 remote-as 65001
 neighbor 192.0.2.254 update-source Loopback0
 address-family evpn
  neighbor 192.0.2.254 activate
  neighbor 192.0.2.254 send-community extended
 address-family ipv4
  network 192.0.2.1/32
end

key_parameters.description: Configures VXLAN interface (single instance per device)
Maps VLAN to VXLAN Network Identifier
Maps VRF to L3 VNI for routing
Anycast gateway IP shared across fabric

concept_summary: EOS supports MPLS with LDP for label distribution and RSVP-TE for traffic engineering. L3VPN services use VRF with BGP VPNv4 address family. Segment Routing provides simplified MPLS without LDP. MPLS support focused on data center interconnect and service provider edge applications. LDP-over-RSVP enables FRR protection.
cli_mode_context: Enable MPLS globally and on interfaces. Configure LDP with 'mpls ldp'. Create VRFs with RD/RT for L3VPN.
example_commands:
configure
mpls ip
mpls ldp router-id Loopback0
interface Ethernet1
 mpls ip
interface Ethernet2
 mpls ip
vrf instance CUSTOMER-A
 rd 65001:100
 route-target import 65001:100
 route-target export 65001:100
interface Ethernet10
 vrf CUSTOMER-A
 ip address 198.51.100.1/24
router bgp 65001
 vrf CUSTOMER-A
  rd 65001:100
  route-target import evpn 65001:100
  route-target export evpn 65001:100
  redistribute connected
 address-family vpn-ipv4
  neighbor 192.0.2.254 activate
end

key_parameters.description: Enables MPLS globally and on interfaces
Route Distinguisher for unique VPN routes

concept_summary: EOS provides HA through MLAG (Multi-Chassis Link Aggregation) for active-active forwarding and redundancy. MLAG peers share control plane while maintaining independent data planes. Configuration sync ensures consistency. Hitless upgrades with ISSU minimize downtime. Modular architecture with process-level fault isolation. Virtual ARP provides gateway redundancy in VXLAN fabrics.
cli_mode_context: Configure MLAG under 'mlag configuration'. Define peer link, domain ID, and local/peer IPs. Configure port-channels with mlag ID.
example_commands:
configure
vlan 4094
 name MLAG-Peer
 trunk group MLAG-Peer
interface Vlan4094
 ip address 10.255.255.1/30
interface Port-Channel1
 description MLAG-Peer-Link
 switchport mode trunk
 switchport trunk group MLAG-Peer
mlag configuration
 domain-id MLAG-DOMAIN-1
 local-interface Vlan4094
 peer-address 10.255.255.2
 peer-link Port-Channel1
interface Port-Channel10
 description MLAG-to-Server
 mlag 10
end

concept_summary: EOS system management includes configuration persistence with startup-config, software upgrades via SWI images, and event monitoring. CloudVision provides centralized management at scale. EOS-as-a-service delivers zero-touch provisioning and streaming telemetry. Configuration can be backed up to flash, USB, or remote servers. Running EOS on Linux enables powerful scripting and automation.
cli_mode_context: Save config with 'write memory'. View configs with 'show running-config'. Install software with 'install source' or boot system commands. Access Linux shell with 'bash'.
example_commands:
configure
end
copy running-config startup-config
write memory
show running-config
show startup-config
install source flash:EOS-4.32.1F.swi
show boot-config
boot system flash:EOS-4.32.1F.swi
dir flash:
show version
show reload cause
bash
df -h
exit
reload
reload in 5

key_parameters.description: Shows software version and hardware info
